2. The relevant fact giving rise to this Rule, in short, is that one Nekjan Nessa, mother of the plaintiffs purchased the suit property from Shahjahan Mollah by a registered deed on 23-4-1887 and during the survey operation of cadastral Survey, the property was wrongly recorded and published in the name of her husband namely, Riazuddin under Khatian Nos. 127, 255 and 323. After the death of Riazuddin Sheikh his son namely, Manik Mollah instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 403 of 1916 in the concerned court. One Nekjan Nesa was the defendant No. 7 in the said suit and the entire property of Nekjan Nessa made over to her by compromise decree in the said suit. One Asiruddin purchased the suit property from Nekjannesa by a registered deed dated 10-3-1917. During the survey operation of State Acquisition, the record had been recorded and published in equal share in the name of Asir Uddin and his full brother Tasir Uddin under Khatian No. 337. Tasiruddin had no right, title and interest in the portion of the suit property. Asiruddin had been possessing the entire property. The plaintiffs became the owner by succession after the death of Asiruddin. During the survey operation of revisional survey, the name of Asiruddin had been correctly recorded and published and the successors of Asiruddin had been possessing the suit property peacefully. The descendent of Taseruddin sold out the property to defendant Nos. 1-3 by a registered deed dated 3-12-1995. Thereafter, they had been threatening the plaintiffs to dispossess from the suit property and, as such, the plaintiffs instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 2 of 1996 for permanent injunction against the defendant. After receiving the show cause notice of temporary injunction, the defendants erected a Shapra (ছাপড়া) just South West portion of the suit plot and fill up the western portion by cutting earth from the east portion and raised a but on it and, as such, dispossessed the plaintiffs from the suit property on 22-1-1996. Hence, the suit for declaration of title and Khan possession of the suit property. 

 16. Order VII, rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure clearly stated that where the subject matter of the suit land is immovable property, the plaint shall contain a description of the property sufficient to identify it, and, in case such property can be identified by boundaries or numbers in a record of settlement of survey, the plaint shall specify such boundaries or numbers.
